events.text:
I built the Live Control web page and tested it locally, but it can't act inside a real Zoom meeting yet, so T-226 is blocked on one yes/no question to Adi. Committed as b75b351.

**What's built.** The page lives in the centre admin, behind a "Live Control" link in the top bar. Anyone on the team with the admin link can use it.
- **Run sheet:** a separate list for each day of timed chat posts, links and polls, which the team can add to, edit and delete.
- **Live buttons:** lock the room, mute everyone, stop video, launch and end polls, and make someone co-host.
- **Activity log:** shows who pressed what and whether it worked.

Pressing a button queues the action, and a "control seat" inside the meeting carries it out and reports back. The seat doesn't exist yet. Zoom gives the centre no way to post chat, launch polls, mute or set co-hosts in a running meeting, so something has to sit in the meeting to do it.

**How it was tested.** I ran the centre locally with a fake Day 2 session 13 minutes in:
- Run-sheet items queued once each when their minute came.
- A second request from the seat got nothing back, so nothing posts twice.
- Bad input is refused: a non-https link, an empty message, a wrong seat key.
- The page renders cleanly on desktop and phone, with no console errors.

Not tested yet: creating polls in Zoom (the poll permissions aren't on the Zoom app) and the seat itself, which doesn't exist.

**What Adi needs to answer.** May I do these three things?
1. Create the Zoom Meeting SDK app "Tantra Live Control" and save its keys in the centre.
2. Add the five poll permissions to the existing Tantra Centre Zoom app.
3. Deploy the centre with a new key so the seat can connect.

If yes, I'll build the seat itself as a small Mac app that opens before each session. Adi will still need to make the seat co-host with one click in Zoom each session. Zoom lets only the host make other people co-host, so the people listed as co-hosts will also need Adi's click, unless he decides to pay for a second Zoom licence.

Reviewers are Adi, Aquila and Bharath (added because this is development work), and note W-ecf15b3b43 is acknowledged. A local copy of the centre is still running so the page can be opened.

Open the page: http://127.0.0.1:8811/admin/enter?k=t226admin, then go to /admin/control?v=t226
